q: 201. The duty of irrigation water will be less if
explain: Duty = Area / Discharge. If a crop requires more water (higher discharge), the same volume of water will cover less area, resulting in a lower duty.

q: 202. The relation between duty (D) in hectares/cumec, delta ($\Delta$) in meters and base period (B) in days is
explain: The standard engineering formula derived from volume calculations: $\Delta = (8.64 \times B) / D$.

q: 203. The area in which crop is grown at a particular time or crop season, is called
explain: The correct term for the area actually being cropped at a specific time is 'Net Sown Area' or 'Irrigated Area' during that season (none of the provided options).

q: 204. The first watering before sowing the crop, is known as
explain: Paleo irrigation is the watering done to the dry land before sowing to provide sufficient moisture for germination.

q: 205. The crops require maximum water during
options: first watering before sowing the crops
first watering when the crop has grown a few centimeters
explain: The 'Kor' watering—the first watering after the plant has grown a few centimeters—usually requires the maximum depth of water.

q: 206. The maximum depth in soil strata, in which the crop spreads its root system, and derives water from the soil, is called
explain: Root zone depth determines the reservoir of moisture available to the plant; irrigation is designed to replenish this specific depth.

q: 207. The depth of root zone is 90 cm for
explain: Wheat is typically categorized as having a root zone depth of approximately 90 cm in design calculations.

q: 208. The duty of a crop is 432 hectares per cumec when the base period of the crop is 100 days. The delta for the crop will be
explain: Using $\Delta = 8.64 B/D$: $\Delta = (8.64 \times 100) / 432 = 2$ meters = 200 cm.

q: 209. The average delta of rice crop is nearly
explain: Rice is a water-intensive crop requiring standing water; its total delta usually ranges between 110 cm to 125 cm.

q: 210. The average duty for sugar-cane in hectares/cumec is
explain: Sugar cane is a perennial crop; while it uses a lot of water, its duty is often calculated around 800 hectares/cumec over its long base period.

q: 211. The optimum depth of kor watering is 19 cm for
explain: The standard kor depth for Rice is 19 cm, whereas for Wheat it is 13.5 cm.

q: 212. Outlet discharge for a particular crop is given by
explain: Discharge = Area / Duty. In this context, 'Outlet factor' is another term for duty at the outlet.

q: 213. The optimum depth of kor watering for wheat in the plains
explain: The kor depth for wheat is standardized at 13.5 cm, which is the first watering after the plants have grown about 2 to 3 centimeters.

q: 214. The kor depth for rice is 19 cm and kor period is 14 days. The outlet factor for the crop in hectares per cumec will be
explain: Outlet factor (Duty) = 8.64B/Δ. Given B = 14 days and Δ = 0.19 m, Duty = (8.64 × 14) / 0.19 ≈ 636.63, rounded to 637.

q: 215. Where steep land is a available, the method of irrigation adopted is
explain: Free flooding (or wild flooding) is used on steep or irregular land where creating borders or checks is not economically feasible.

q: 216. For closed growing crops (such as wheat), the method of irrigation used is
explain: Border flooding is very effective for close-growing crops like wheat or barley because it provides uniform distribution over long strips.

q: 217. Check flooding method of irrigation is used for
options: crops which can stand inundation of water for sometime
crops such as sugarcane, potatoes etc.
explain: Check flooding involves surrounding plots with low levees; it is ideal for heavy soils or crops like rice that can handle standing water.

q: 218. Sprinkler irrigation is adopted for ............. areas.
explain: Sprinkler irrigation is highly versatile for uneven or undulating topography where surface irrigation would require expensive land leveling.

q: 219. The method of irrigation used for orchards is
explain: In basin flooding, a circular or square basin is formed around each tree or group of trees, which is common in orchard management.

q: 220. The science which deals with the physical features and conditions of water on the earth surface is called
explain: Hydrography is the study of physical features of bodies of water and their adjacent land areas.

q: 221. The earth's water circulatory system, is known as
explain: The hydrologic cycle describes the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the Earth.

q: 222. The fall of moisture from the atmosphere to the earth surface in any form, is called
explain: Precipitation includes rain, snow, hail, and sleet—essentially any moisture falling from the clouds.

q: 223. Liquid precipitation consists of
explain: Among the options, only rainfall is in a purely liquid state when it reaches the ground.

q: 224. The precipitation caused by natural rising of warmer lighter air colder and denser surroundings is called
explain: Convective precipitation occurs when the earth's surface is heated, causing warm air to rise, cool, and condense into rain.

q: 225. The precipitation caused by lifting of warm moisture laden air masses due to topographic barriers is called
explain: Orographic precipitation occurs when air is forced to rise over mountains or hills, leading to cooling and rainfall on the windward side.

q: 226. The process of loosing water from the leaves of plants, is termed as
explain: Transpiration is the biological process where water is taken up by roots and released as vapor through leaf stomata.

q: 227. The amount of precipitation is measured by
explain: A rain gauge is the standard instrument used to gather and measure the amount of liquid precipitation over a set period.

q: 228. The commonly used rain gauge is
explain: The tipping bucket rain gauge is widely used in automated weather stations for its ability to transmit data electronically.

q: 229. The standard height of a standard rain gauge is
explain: Standard rain gauges are typically installed so the rim is 30 cm above the ground to avoid splash-in from the surrounding soil.

q: 230. A graph showing variations of discharge with time, at a particular point of a stream is known as
explain: A hydrograph plots the river discharge (flow rate) against time, showing how a stream responds to rainfall.

q: 231. A hydrograph representing one cm of runoff from a rainfall of some unit duration and specific area distribution is known as
explain: The unit hydrograph is a fundamental tool in hydrology representing the response of a watershed to 1 cm of effective rainfall.

q: 232. Run-off is measure in
explain: Run-off rate (discharge) is conventionally measured in cubic meters per second (cumecs).

q: 233. A canal aligned nearly parallel to the contours of a country, is known is
explain: A contour canal follows the natural contours, allowing it to irrigate the land on the downhill side.

q: 234. A canal aligned approximately parallel to the natural drainage of a country is a called
explain: Side slope canals are aligned perpendicular to contours (parallel to drainage lines) to avoid crossing natural drains.

q: 235. The water shed canal is also called
explain: A ridge canal (watershed canal) is aligned along the highest ridge line, allowing gravity irrigation on both sides.

q: 236. Irrigation canals are generally aligned along
explain: Aligning along the watershed (ridge) is preferred because it eliminates the need for expensive cross-drainage works.

q: 237. A canal aligned at right angles to contour of a country, is known as
explain: Side slope canals run roughly at right angles to the contours.

q: 238. The alignment of a canal
options: should ensure minimum cross drainage works
on a water shed is the most economical
explain: Canal alignment is a multi-objective process balancing cost, drainage crossings, and social/environmental impact.

q: 239. Inundation canals draw their supplies from rivers whenever there is
explain: Inundation canals do not have a headwork (weir/barrage) and only receive water when the river level rises during floods.

q: 240. A contour canal
options: is most suitable is hilly areas
is aligned parallel to the contour of the country
explain: Contour canals are common in hills; since they follow the terrain elevation, they can only deliver water to the side that is lower in elevation.

q: 241. Which of the following is the correct sequence of the parts of a canal system?
options: Head works, distributary, branch canals and minor
Head works, main canal, branch canal, distributary and minor
Head works, main canal, branch canal, branch canal, minor and distributary
explain: The standard hierarchy is Main Canal → Branch Canal → Distributary → Minor → Watercourse.

q: 242. The narrow strip of land left at the ground level between the inner toe of the bank and top edge of the cutting, is known as
explain: Berms act as a buffer to prevent bank erosion and provide space for future widening of the canal.

q: 243. The berms when fully formed
options: reduce the absorption losses and prevents leaks
protect the bank from erosion because of wave action
provide a scope for future widening the channel
explain: Berms collect silt over time, which helps in lining the canal naturally (reducing seepage) and strengthening the banks.

q: 244. The free board in a channel is governed by the
explain: Freeboard is the safety margin between the full supply level and the top of the bank to prevent overtopping.

q: 245. The saturation gradient in an ordinary loam soils is, usually, kept from
explain: The saturation line (phreatic line) in loam soil banks is typically assumed to have a slope of 4:1 for design stability.

q: 246. The height of dowel above the road level should not be more than
explain: A dowel is a small curb on the canal bank road to prevent vehicles from falling; 30 cm is the standard maximum height.

q: 247. The width of dowel is, usually, kept from
explain: Dowels typically range from 0.3 to 0.6 meters in width to remain stable and functional as a safety curb.

q: 248. A spoil bank is formed when the
options: volume of excavation is in excess of the embankment filling
explain: When the earth excavated from the canal is more than what is needed for the banks, the surplus is piled into 'spoil banks'.

q: 249. The borrow pits should, preferably, be taken from
options: the field on the right side of canal
the field on the left side of the canal
the central half width of the section of the canal
explain: Taking borrow pits from the canal bed (central width) is preferred because they will eventually fill with silt, making the canal bed smoother.

q: 250. In case of small channels, the borrow pits should start from a distance not less than ............. from the toe of the embankment.
explain: A safe distance (minimum 5m) is maintained to prevent the borrow pit from undermining the stability of the canal embankment.

q: 251. When the quantity of the earth is much in excess of the quantity required for filling, it has to be deposited in the form of spoil banks. The spoil banks are made on
explain: Depending on available land and the volume of excess soil, spoil banks can be constructed on either or both sides of the canal alignment.

q: 252. A land is said to be water-logged when
options: the air circulation is stopped in the root zone due to the rise in water table
the soil pores within a depth of 40 cm are saturated
explain: Waterlogging occurs when the water table rises to the root zone, displacing air and preventing the oxygen circulation necessary for plant growth.

q: 253. The infertility of the soil in water-logged areas is due to
options: inhibiting activity of the soil bacteria
explain: Waterlogging leads to anaerobic conditions (killing aerobic bacteria), salt accumulation (salinization), and the proliferation of water-loving weeds.

q: 254. Water logging is caused due to
explain: It is generally caused by a combination of excessive water input (rain/irrigation) and the inability of that water to drain away naturally or artificially.

q: 255. The soil becomes, practically, infertile if its pH value is
explain: A pH of 11 indicates highly alkaline (sodic) soil, which is toxic to most crops and destroys soil structure.

q: 256. The measure adopted to reclaim the water-logged area is
explain: Reclamation involves reducing water input (lining) and removing excess groundwater (lift irrigation/pumping) or adjusting canal levels.

q: 257. Lining of a canal is necessary
options: to minimize the seepage losses in canal
to prevent erosion of bed and sides due to high velocities
to increase the discharge in canal section by increasing the velocity
explain: Lining creates a smooth, impermeable surface that saves water, allows for higher non-erodible velocities, and improves discharge capacity.

q: 258. Lining of canal ............. the maintenance of the canal.
explain: Lining prevents weed growth and silting, which significantly reduces the frequency and cost of annual maintenance.

q: 259. Lining of a canal
options: increases available head for power generation
explain: A lined canal is more stable, loses less water to seepage, and maintains a steeper energy gradient useful for small-scale hydro projects.

q: 260. The sodium carbonate lining consists of at least
explain: A low-cost lining method involves mixing approximately 1% sodium carbonate with 6% clay into the soil to reduce permeability.

q: 261. For the repairing of an old but sound concrete lining, the lining preferred is
explain: Shotcrete (pneumatically applied mortar) is ideal for repairing cracks or resurfacing existing concrete structures.

q: 262. The weed growth in a canal leads to
explain: Weeds increase the rugosity (roughness) of the channel, which slows down the water velocity and reduces the overall discharge capacity.

q: 263. Kennedy, in his silt theory, assumed that the silt is kept in suspension because of eddies generated from the
explain: Kennedy's theory simplified the mechanics by assuming only the vertical eddies rising from the canal bed support the silt particles.

q: 264. Kennedy gave a relation between
options: critical velocity and the depth of flowing water
explain: Kennedy's fundamental equation ($V_0 = 0.55D^{0.64}$) relates the critical velocity (no silting, no scouring) to the depth of water ($D$).

q: 265. The relation given by Kennedy for critical velocity in m/s is
explain: This is the standard formula where 'm' is the critical velocity ratio and 'D' is the depth.

q: 266. A channel is said to be in scouring when the critical velocity ratio is ............. one.
explain: If the CVR ($m$) is greater than 1, the actual velocity is higher than the critical velocity required to prevent scouring, leading to bed erosion.

q: 267. According to Kennedy, the silt transporting power of a channel is proportional to
explain: Kennedy derived that the silt carrying capacity of a channel varies with the 2.5 (or 5/2) power of its velocity.

q: 268. According to Lacey, a channel is said to be in regime, if
options: it flows in incoherent unlimited alluvium of the same character as that transported material
the silt grade and the silt charge are constant
explain: Lacey's 'True Regime' conditions require constant discharge, constant silt properties, and flow through an unlimited alluvial bed.

q: 269. The main cause of silting in channel is
explain: Silting occurs when velocity drops (due to poor slope or design) or when excessive silt enters through the head regulator.

q: 270. According to Lacey
options: the silt is kept in suspension due to the force of vertical eddies
the eddies are generated from bed and sides, both normal to the surface of generation
the vertical component of eddies generated from sides will also support the silt
explain: Unlike Kennedy, Lacey accounted for eddies generated from the entire wetted perimeter (bed and sides).

q: 271. Lacey assumed that silt is kept in suspension because of the normal components of eddies generated from the
explain: Lacey's theory improved upon Kennedy's by stating that eddies arise from the whole perimeter, including the sides.

q: 272. Lacey gave a relation between
explain: Lacey provided a comprehensive set of equations relating $V$, $R$, $A$, $Q$, and $S$ for regime channels.

q: 273. The channel after attaining its section and longitudinal slope, will be said to be in ............. regime.
explain: Final regime is the state reached when a channel has adjusted its perimeter, depth, and slope to become stable in alluvium.

q: 274. The general regime flow equation is
explain: This is Lacey's general flow equation derived for regime channels in alluvium.

q: 275. If m is the mean particle diameter of the silt in mm, the Lacey's silt factor (f) is given by
explain: The silt factor $f$ determines the roughness and required velocity of the channel based on the bed material size.

q: 276. Distributary head regulators are provided
options: to control the supplies to the off-taking channel
to control the silt entry in the off-taking canal
to stop the supply, when not needed, in the off-taking canal
explain: These regulators act as valves to manage discharge, sediment intake, and closure for the smaller off-taking canal.

q: 277. Cross regulators are provided
options: to raise the water level to its upstream during the periods of low discharges in the parent channel
to help in closing the supply to downstream of the parent channel
to absorb fluctuation in various sections of the canal system
explain: Cross regulators are built across the main canal to back up water for off-takes and control flow downstream.

q: 278. A structure constructed in an irrigation canal for the purpose of wasting some of its water, is known as a
explain: Escapes act as safety valves to discharge excess water caused by heavy rain or sudden closures of off-takes.

q: 279. Escapes are also known as ............. for the canals.
explain: They protect the canal banks from overtopping and breaching during emergency conditions.

q: 280. The capacity of escape channel should not be less than ............. of the capacity of the parent channel at that point.
explain: To be effective as an emergency safety structure, an escape must be able to handle at least 50% of the canal's design discharge.

q: 281. A fall, which maintains the depth is a
explain: A trapezoidal notch fall is designed so that the depth-discharge relationship of the fall matches the canal itself, maintaining constant depth.

q: 282. The Sarda canal has a
explain: The Sarda type fall is a classic example of a vertical drop fall, used when the discharge is small and the drop is around 1 to 1.5 meters.

q: 283. In Sarda type fall, the length of the crest is kept ............. the bed width of the canal.
explain: Standard design for a Sarda fall keeps the crest length equal to the bed width of the incoming canal.

q: 284. In a Sarda type fall, the width of the trapezoidal crest (B) is given by
explain: This empirical formula is used to calculate the stable top width of the crest for a trapezoidal Sarda fall.

q: 285. The relation for discharge (Q) over a rectangular crest of a Sarda fall is
explain: This is the modified weir formula used for the rectangular crest design of a Sarda type fall.

q: 286. A baffle wall is a sort of low weir constructed at the end of the cistern to
options: head up water to its upstream to such a high that hydraulic jump is formed
withstand the actual impact of the high velocity jet to dissipate the energy
explain: The baffle wall (or baffle platform) helps ensure the hydraulic jump occurs within the paved cistern to protect the bed.

q: 287. A parabolic glacis type fall is commonly known as
explain: The Montague fall utilizes a parabolic glacis to efficiently guide water into the cistern and promote energy dissipation.

q: 288. When the water is thrown into a well over a crest from where it escapes near its bottom, the type of fall is called
explain: A cylinder fall (well fall) uses a vertical shaft to drop water, making it suitable for very large drops and small discharges.

q: 289. A sudden fall of level of ground along the alignment of a canal joined by an inclined bed is called a
explain: Rapid falls consist of a long sloping glacis and are used where the natural ground slope is steeper than the canal bed slope.

q: 290. The cylinder or well fall is quite suitable and economical for
explain: Well falls are ideal for dropping small amounts of water over high vertical distances, such as in hilly terrain.

q: 291. The discharge (Q) over trapezoidal crest of Sarda fall is ............. as compared to rectangular crest of identical parameters.
explain: Due to the wider side area in a trapezoidal shape, the discharge capacity is slightly higher than a rectangular crest of the same base width.

q: 292. The Ingles type fall makes use of ............. impact for energy dissipation.
explain: The Ingles (or baffle) fall uses a vertical impact of the water jet against a baffle wall to dissipate kinetic energy.

q: 293. The fall which can be used as meter fall, is
explain: A flumed glacis fall can be calibrated to accurately measure the discharge passing through it.

q: 294. A canal outlet should
options: be so designed that the farmer cannot temper with its functioning
be simple so that it can be constructed or fabricated by local masons
draw its fair share of silt carried by the distributing channel
explain: A good outlet (module) must be tamper-proof, simple, and proportional in silt and water distribution.

q: 295. A device which ensures a constant discharge of water passing from one channel to another irrespective of water level in each within certain specified limits, is called
explain: This is the definition of a rigid module, which provides a constant discharge regardless of water level fluctuations.

q: 296. An outlet in which the discharge depends upon the difference in level between the water levels in distributing channel and the water course, is known as
explain: Non-modular outlets (like a simple pipe) vary their discharge based on the water levels of both the parent canal and the field channel.

q: 297. In a flexible outlet, the discharge depends upon the
options: difference of water level between distributary and water course
explain: A semi-module (flexible outlet) depends only on the water level in the parent distributary, not on the field channel level.

q: 298. When discharge of an outlet is independent of the water levels in the water course and the distributary, the outlet is termed as a
explain: A rigid module is designed to provide a fixed flow rate even if water levels change in either channel.

q: 299. In a proportional outlet, the rate of change of its discharge is ............. the rate of change of the discharge of the distributing channel.
explain: Proportionality means that if the parent canal discharge increases by 10%, the outlet discharge also increases by 10%.

q: 300. The ratio of the head recovered to the head put in an outlet, is called
explain: Efficiency of an outlet refers to how much energy (head) is maintained after the water passes through the module.
